propertyFacts.label: Absolute Photoluminescence Quantum Yield
propertyFacts.scope: Same QD formulation measured in thin-film form on a cleaned glass slide; not proven to be the NP5 ITO film. Main p.2 calls this an integrating-sphere thin-film QY. SI p.14 names the Hamamatsu C9920-02/C10027 system specifically for the separate toluene-solution absolute-QY measurement; the film's instrument is not identified separately. The solution N2 purge and 6.7/6.8% QYs are not assigned to this film.

source_locator.locator: SI PDF p.14, Supporting Information 9

propertyFacts.label: Calculated Photoluminescence Quantum Yield
propertyFacts.scope: QD region near NP5, 405 nm excitation; authors calculated QY using measured lifetime and thin-film baseline. SI p.8 derives these values from the near-prism lifetime, initial-intensity radiative-rate enhancement and separate thin-film 3.00% QY baseline; this is calculated, not direct single-prism absolute QY.

intuition.title: Why excitation wavelength matters
intuition.text: Near one Ag nanoprism, 405 and 470 nm excitation give different measured PL intensity and authors’ calculated quantum yields; modeled resonance curves are comparison evidence, not measured structure.

scopeLabel: Independent scoped quick audit of main pp.1–4, Figures 1–2 and Table 1, plus essential SI pp.1–2,5,13–14. Upstream QD and Ag nanoprism syntheses are cited inputs only.

general_background.title: Thermodynamics and kinetics
general_background.summary: Thermodynamics describes which states are energetically favoured, while kinetics governs how quickly a system can move between them. A change can be favourable yet proceed slowly when an activation barrier or limited transport restricts the pathway.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation
